coaching_cues: Attach ankle strap to low cable
Keep the working knee aligned with the standing knee — don't flare it
don't let the weight snap the leg straight
common_mistakes: Swinging the hip to complete the rep
Not fully extending the leg on the eccentric
Using too much weight — hamstrings are strong, but isolation requires control
before.pro_tip: Single-leg version addresses side-to-side hamstring imbalances that prone leg curl misses; great rehab and prehab tool

coaching_cues: Stand tall on one leg, hips square, touching a wall for balance if you need it
Curl the heel toward your glute, thigh staying vertical
Pause at the top, lower for a slow count of two
common_mistakes: Swinging the hip to complete the rep
Not fully extending the leg on the way down
Letting the thigh drift forward as the heel comes up
Dropping the leg instead of lowering it
after.pro_tip: Trains one hamstring at a time, so it shows up side-to-side imbalances a two-legged curl hides. Slow the lowering to 3 seconds once 15 clean reps per leg feel easy
